def larg_nnum(lst, n):
    """
    Returns a set containing the n largest items from the given list.
    
    Args:
        lst (list): The input list of numbers.
        n (int): The number of largest items to return.
        
    Returns:
        set: A set of the n largest unique items found in the list.
    """
    if not isinstance(n, int) or n <= 0:
        raise ValueError("n must be a positive integer.")
    
    # Sort the list in descending order to easily pick the largest elements
    sorted_lst = sorted(lst, reverse=True)
    
    # Slice the top n elements. 
    # Note: If there are fewer than n items, it will just return all available ones.
    top_n_elements = sorted_lst[:n]
    
    # Convert to a set as per the assertion requirement (to handle duplicates like 20 and 50)
    result_set = set(top_n_elements)
    
    return result_set

# Test cases based on your example
if __name__ == "__main__":
    input_list = [10, 20, 50, 70, 90, 20, 50, 40, 60, 80, 100]
    
    # The assertion checks if the set of top 2 numbers is {100, 90}
    assert set(larg_nnum(input_list, 2)) == set([100, 90]), "Test failed!"
    
    print("All tests passed.")
